newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Coffee rally extends then meets profit-takers.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Coffee rally extends then meets profit-takers.

text.p: A technical sell-off blunted the week's rally in world coffee prices on Friday but not before US July futures for the arabica type of beans hit a new contract high at $2.25 per pound.

The market then tumbled a dizzy 11 cents in just 30 minutes before edging up again. The downturn was viewed as a technical correction to the recent explosive rally. Current values compare with around $1 back in December.
But the July contract's ability to rebuff a test of chart resistance at $2.25 and fears the market was well overbought sparked waves of speculative liquidation.
"The market went up 30 cents in four days and it was overdue for a correction," one trader said. "It's shaken up the confidence of some longs and got them ready to take profits."
The rally on arabica coffee was reignited this week by concerns about tight Latin American supply and the onset of the Brazilian frost season.
Smaller-than-expected harvests in some Latin American countries, notably Colombia, and the prospect of a disappointing crop in Brazil in the 1997/98 season underpinned prices, traders say.
German roasters (processors) have begun a new round of retail price increases in reaction to the gains in arabica futures and following an increase by Folgers of the United States.
Market leader Kraft Jacobs Suchard said it would probably announce price hikes of roasted coffee within the next week.
The German number two, Tchibo Frisch-Roest Kaffee GmbH, added up to one mark to each packet of the high quality coffee on sale in its 20,000 shops.
London futures for robusta beans, used in making soluble or instant coffee, are up by one-third since the start of 1997 at around $1,650 per tonne on Friday.
But they are more generously supplied and the London market has not been so dramatic as New York this week.
Chicago soybeans futures again sprinted higher on Friday on strong US demand but benchmark Chicago wheat futures eased on profit-taking after the latest weather-led rally.
Gold and London base metals prices were generally little changed but crude oil eased.
The benchmark Brent Blend of crude for July traded in London just below $18 per barrel, about 50 cents down from Thursday afternoon.
But traders said this was little changed from early this week and that crude was within a range in a balanced market.
London markets are closed for a holiday on Monday and the next London report in this series will appear on Tuesday, May 6.
